edges.mechanism: Dietary broccoli (500 g/d) induced CYP1A2 (caffeine metabolic ratio +19%); SFN itself did not alter CYP1A2 in human hepatocytes, so supplement-level relevance is uncertain.
edges.evidence: Human controlled diet study of whole broccoli (n=16) plus in vitro human hepatocytes; low certainty for supplements.

edges.mechanism: SFN decreased CYP3A4 expression/activity in human hepatocytes in vitro; in vivo 450 umol SFN did not change midazolam clearance overall (decrease only in highest-baseline subset).
edges.evidence: In vitro plus one human randomized crossover (n=24) largely null; low certainty, likely not clinically important.

edges.mechanism: SFN is a human PXR antagonist in vitro but did not attenuate rifampicin-induced CYP3A4 induction in vivo.
edges.evidence: Human randomized crossover (n=24); no interaction demonstrated.

edges.mechanism: Nrf2-mediated induction of UGT1A1/1A8/1A10 could theoretically increase glucuronidation of co-administered drugs.
edges.evidence: In vitro (Caco-2) only; theoretical.

edges.mechanism: Nrf2 activation in tumour cells may upregulate drug-detoxification pathways and contribute to chemoresistance; direction is context-dependent and SFN is also being trialled as a doxorubicin cardioprotectant.
edges.evidence: Preclinical/review evidence and ongoing trial; no human outcome data on interference.

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose lowering: SFN suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis via NRF2 and lowered fasting glucose/HbA1c in T2D and fasting glucose modestly in prediabetes.
edges.evidence: Human trials of SFN alone (T2D trial; RCT n=74); combination not studied; theoretical additive effect.

edges.mechanism: Both reduce hepatic glucose output; SFN effect in diabetic animals was of similar magnitude to metformin; additive glucose lowering possible.
edges.evidence: Animal comparison plus human SFN-alone data; combination not studied.

edges.mechanism: Theoretical additive glucose lowering (different mechanism: SFN reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis).
edges.evidence: Extrapolated from SFN-alone human glycaemic trials; no combination data.

edges.mechanism: Reduced gastric acidity spared co-delivered myrosinase and increased GR-to-SFN conversion (higher SFN metabolite excretion on omeprazole).
edges.evidence: Small human pilot pharmacokinetic study.

edges.mechanism: Adjunctive SFN with antipsychotics (incl. risperidone) improved negative symptoms/irritability modestly, lowered discontinuation and lipids; no adverse PK interaction reported.
edges.evidence: Several small RCTs and a 2025 SR/MA (4 RCTs, n=369); low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Adjunctive SFN improved ADHD-RS scores with comparable side-effect frequency.
edges.evidence: Single RCT (n=70); very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: BroccoMax formulation contains calcium ascorbate; ascorbic acid co-administered with GR in myrosinase bioavailability trial; separate contribution to conversion not quantified.
edges.evidence: Label composition and one randomized crossover where both arms received ascorbate; overlap rather than proven synergy.

edges.mechanism: Both are Nrf2 inducers; combination induced skin NQO1 3.6-fold vs 3.1 (GR) and 3.3 (curcumin).
edges.evidence: Small randomized mechanistic trial (n=6/arm); no clinical outcomes.

edges.with: mustard seed / raw cruciferous myrosinase sources
edges.mechanism: Exogenous plant myrosinase hydrolyses glucoraphanin to sulforaphane, doubling SFN bioavailability from GR-only extract.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover (n=16) and human bioavailability studies.

edges.mechanism: Glucosinolate goitrogen concern; SFN itself not the goitrogenic species (goitrin/thiocyanate are), and a 12-wk RCT showed no change in TSH, fT4, thyroglobulin or autoimmunity.
edges.evidence: RCT (n=45) and 2024 SR: reassuring, especially with adequate iodine; long-term high-dose data in thyroid disease lacking.

edges.mechanism: Goitrogenic glucosinolate breakdown products matter mainly when iodine intake is inadequate.
edges.evidence: 2024 SR of 123 studies; low-certainty concern.

edges.mechanism: Limited human data (small dose-escalation study in pregnancy hypertension); label advises consulting a professional.
edges.evidence: Small uncontrolled/crossover study (n=12 pregnant); label warning.

edges.mechanism: Higher BMI associated with lower or altered GR-to-SFN conversion and absorption.
edges.evidence: Human pharmacokinetic studies (pilot and RCT n=18).

edges.mechanism: GSTM1-null subjects had slightly higher plasma SFN-metabolite AUC and faster early excretion; prostate gene-expression responses differed by genotype.
edges.evidence: Randomized crossover (n=16) and 12-month RCT; significance for outcomes unknown.

edges.mechanism: Plasma SFN higher in GSTT1-null individuals; benzene mercapturic acid excretion lower in GSTT1-null regardless of treatment.
edges.evidence: Secondary analyses of RCTs (n=105, n=291).

edges.mechanism: Glucose-lowering effect (fasting glucose, HbA1c) may change glycaemic control.
edges.evidence: Human trials in T2D and prediabetes; low certainty.
